_comment: Which PRD artefact schema versions the toolchain still claims to accept, and which one
is current. Item 43. Two rules keep this set from rotting:
1. One fixture per schema version the toolchain still ACCEPTS. Dropping read support
drops the fixture -- otherwise the directory grows for ever and most of it is
decoration.
2. A non-current fixture is FROZEN. It changes only when the migration's expected
output changes. If the fixture project needs a fourth feature to exercise
something new, that is a reason to touch the current schema only. Maintaining the
same project twice is the cost that makes people abandon versioned fixtures.
The frozen hashes below are what enforces rule 2. They are not a security measure --
anyone can update them -- they are a speed bump that turns an accidental edit into a
failing check with a name on it.
frozen_sha256 = sha256 over every file in the version directory, in sorted
relative-POSIX-path order, hashing `path + NUL + bytes + NUL` for each. The suite
recomputes it and prints the actual digest when it disagrees, so a DELIBERATE change
to a frozen fixture is a copy-paste and an accidental one is a named failure.
judgement_elements = the elements a MIXED step's migration may not produce, because
assigning them is a judgement the guide forbids a machine to make. The golden
comparison strips these before comparing, so it asserts exactly what the script was
supposed to do and nothing about what it was forbidden to do.
A non-current fixture is not decoration under these rules: it is the INPUT to item 41's
migration test and to item 24's compatibility comparison, so it is exercised on every
run rather than merely stored.

schema-1.description: The schema as shipped in plugin 2.0.0: <criterion> with given/when/then, MoSCoW priority duplicated between index and feature file, and a feature's definition completeness recorded in a <status> element sharing its name with three other things.
schema-1.notes: Superseded by schema-2 at item 45. Kept because it is the INPUT to item 41's migration comparison and the only artefact of an older schema in the repository -- which is what item 24's 'refuse on a known incompatibility' needs to be testable at all.

schema-2.description: Item 45's rename: a PRD feature's <status> becomes <definition>, a CRD's <meta><status> becomes <workflow>, and PROJECT.md's <feature status=> becomes built=. Values are unchanged; only the tags differ, so a diff against schema-1 shows the rename and nothing else.
schema-2.notes: link-shelf is the §5.1 end-to-end fixture; staff-service is item 21's tier probe. Both carried over from schema-1 with the rename applied and no other edit -- deliberately, so that item 41's golden comparison has exactly one transformation to account for.

schema-3.description: Items 33 and 34: a <criterion> is one EARS sentence carrying `pattern` and `priority`, replacing the Given/When/Then triple. Migrated criteria also carry `derived-from` until sign-off.
schema-3.notes: The first step that is not fully mechanical. `priority` and `derived-from` are the script's; the EARS sentence and its `pattern` are judgements the guide forbids a machine to make, so migrate.py reports PARTIAL and --check refuses the tree. The golden comparison for this step therefore asserts the mechanical half exactly and the judgement half not at all -- see the suite.

schema-4.description: Items 1, 2, 5, 11, 12, 27, 29 and 35: the rest of the feature template, and what-next.md's parseable skeleton. <user-story> before the description, <depends-on slug= kind=> after it, <gaps> between the criteria and the notes, <notes> split into <data-model> and <considerations>, an optional <architecturally-significant> in <meta>, and the duplicated <priority> removed from <meta>. No <phases> element, deliberately.
schema-4.notes: quokka-telemetry is where the specification-gap bar first fires: it carries a <gap kind="specification"> and is therefore in-progress rather than defined. Item 43 recorded that rule as sound in principle and unexercised in fact; this is the fixture exercising it. link-shelf/crd/archive-links.md is the first structured CRD in the corpus and arrives HERE rather than at schema-1: until item 46 the CRD path had nothing this plan had changed, and back-filling it into three frozen versions to give it a history it did not have would have broken rule 2 to buy nothing.

schema-5.description: Items 46, 47 and 48: the CRD path takes the parity changes. <requirements> is retired and each entry becomes a criterion in the single list, renumbered and carrying derived-from="requirement-N"; requirement-level MoSCoW becomes P0|P1|P2 one to one; <meta> gains a document-level MoSCoW <priority>; and <gaps> arrives. PRD features, PROJECT.md and what-next.md are unchanged and are named as unchanged.
schema-5.notes: The first step whose mechanical half MOVES content rather than relabelling it, which is why the criterion-id invariant had to be widened from equality to a prefix -- an existing id must still resolve, but appending is now legitimate. The judgement surface is wide because three of the four changes have no mechanical half at all: the EARS sentence and `pattern` for a migrated requirement, the document tier, and the gaps. A `wont-have` requirement is an ESCALATION rather than a mapping -- P0|P1|P2 has no `not building this` level by design -- and that path is exercised separately from the golden comparison.

planned._comment: Item 11 was listed here as arriving with schema-5 and in fact landed in schema-4, with what-next.md's skeleton. Recorded rather than quietly deleted: a planned entry that turns out to be wrong about WHEN is the normal case, and the correction is the only evidence the entry was ever checked.

_items_16_17.outcome: NOT a schema version, and the prediction that they would be is corrected here rather than deleted.
_items_16_17.why: Items 16 and 17 change the TASK format, and a task is not a versioned artefact. migrate.py recognises five roots -- feature, crd, prd, what-next, project-context -- and a task is none of them, because tasks are regenerable output rather than authored documents: the way to move a task set to a new shape is to re-run /breakdown, not to migrate it. Versioning them would have meant a fixture and a migration step for files nobody ever hand-edits. manifest.json carries its own MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION, which went 1.0 -> 1.1 for item 16's fields, and that is the correct granularity.

schema-6.description: No longer a placeholder: item 40 landed and named exactly one thing it needs from this version. The bar's gate is 'the mechanical tests pass AND a review has been recorded', check-definition.py is the whole of the first half, and no artefact carries anywhere to record the second. Item 38's gate belongs in the same version because it is the other consumer of a recorded judgement.
schema-6.content_work: The reference fixture's `defined` labels predate the bar and four features fail its mechanical tests: link-shelf/list-links (no unwanted-behaviour criterion and no <data-model>), and staff-service/zebra-signin, walrus-export and narwhal-theme (no <data-model>). Fixing the CONTENT rather than the label is what section 4.2 requires -- lowering four <definition> tags to silence a check is the failure mode the gate is deliberately too weak to force. It lands HERE rather than as a quiet edit because the PRD features are byte-identical across schema-1..5, so the fix reaches four frozen fixtures and the migration's golden comparison, and rule 2 says a frozen fixture changes only when the migration's expected output does. Item 22's check adds a fifth file to the same batch: staff-service declares <status>defined</status> at DOCUMENT level in both index.md and what-next.md, and core section 3's enum for that tag is in-progress|complete. Both files agree, so the F3 DISAGREE check passes and nothing had ever validated the value -- which matters because /prd --resume finds incomplete PRDs by that tag, so a PRD saying `defined` is one nothing can classify. Same batch, same reason, same frozen fixtures.
